done_when: A follow-up that names a period the app reads itself (a month with or without a year, a year, a quarter with or without a year, or last, previous or this month, quarter or year) answers for that period whatever window the model emits; fiscal and other wording (FY, YTD, next month, previous week) keeps the model's window and the period control; a question naming no period still inherits or aggregates as before, and an amount is never read as a year; changing an answer's period still re-runs on the chosen period

findings.body: `QUANTITY_OF_YEAR_PATTERN` recognizes only “amount/total/value … of 2025”, while the comparison guard does not recognize the equally explicit form “is 2025”. Consequently, “Show GL codes where Actual amount is 2025” reaches `calendarYear`, which returns 2025 and replaces the model or inherited window with the whole calendar year. This violates the requirement that an amount is never read as a year, and the regression matrix has no scalar `amount is …` case.
findings.title: Not done: An amount phrased with “is” can still be read as a calendar year

findings.body: After stripping the enumerated display/comparison phrases, any remaining bare `quarter` still satisfies `PERIOD_WORD_PATTERN`. For example, “Show a quarter breakdown of Actual” is not parsed by either time-window parser, but `hasTimePeriodWords` returns true, so the model-emitted window is retained and a prior window is not inherited. This question names no specific period and therefore must inherit or aggregate; the added matrix covers “by quarter” and quarter-over-quarter but not this generic granularity wording.
findings.title: Not done: A generic quarter breakdown can preserve the model’s arbitrary window

findings.body: The period matrix and rerun test exercise `ChatService.ask` through `makeFixture`, whose provider, executor/database, audit, dimensions, and resolver are fakes. The registered root suite (`package.json:26`) runs Node/Vitest tests, the frontend suite (`frontend/package.json:9`) is jsdom Vitest, and there is no Playwright specification exercising a browser against the running API and a real database. Thus the named-period override, no-period inheritance/aggregation, amount protection, and edited-period rerun still lack the required end-to-end user-flow proof; the successful close run only establishes the hermetic tests.
findings.title: Not done: end-to-end Ask coverage for period selection and reruns

why: An Ask question that names a period, such as July 2026, answers for that period even as a follow-up in the same thread; the model's own window and the previous answer's window used to win
